newsitem.title: INDIA: India's NHB pays 9.12 bln rupees to ANZ.
newsitem.headline: India's NHB pays 9.12 bln rupees to ANZ.

text.p: India's National Housing Bank (NHB) on Thursday paid 9.12 billion rupees ($255 million) to ANZ Grindlays Bank to comply with an arbitration panel ruling, NHB chairman P.P. Vora said.
The award is linked to securities transactions involving Harshad Mehta, a broker at the centre of the 1992 bull market which had exploded into a scandal.
NHB paid ANZ after a special court ruled that ANZ will have to repay the money if the arbitration ruling is overruled by a higher court, which NHB will be appealing to.
"We paid after the special court (on Thursday) said if (the payment was) set aside, eventually, they (ANZ) will have to return the money," Vora told Reuters.
An executive handling the case at ANZ Grindlays at its Bombay office declined to confirm the payment or comment about the special court's ruling.
In 1992, NHB, a subsidiary of the central bank Reserve Bank of India (RBI), issued nine crossed account payee only cheques favouring ANZ Grindlays, which ANZ credited to Mehta's account.
ANZ was told by the RBI to repay the money to NHB as it sought to unravel Mehta's dealings.
The foreign bank disputed NHB's claim, but agreed to comply with RBI's instruction subject to the case being referred to an arbitration panel.
The panel ordered that NHB repay ANZ Grindlays 5.06 billion rupees, plus interest from 1992.
NHB is expected to appeal to higher courts.
